title: Bioinformatics Specialist
details: Public Health Sciences Division · Matsen Lab
summary: Conceptualized and implemented transformer-based deep amino acid selection models (DASM) of viral protein evolution in PyTorch. Designed and built multidms, a JAX model that jointly fits multiple deep mutational scanning datasets, now used in primary analysis pipelines across multiple labs. Built a Nextflow pipeline that ran 50K+ HPC jobs to produce the primary data for a study published in *Cell*.

highlights.title: Deep selection models for viral protein evolution
highlights.text: Conceptualized and implemented a Deep Amino acid Selection Model (DASM) for viral protein evolution, adapting the lab's transformer-based framework for separating natural selection from mutation from B-cell lineages to viral phylogenies. Built the codon-level training objective and the parent-child data pipeline in PyTorch within the open-source [netam](https://github.com/matsengrp/netam) package. This work is unpublished.

highlights.title: Jointly modeling deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets
highlights.text: Developed a novel approach for jointly modeling multiple distinct DMS experimental datasets. The method was validated *in-silico* (using simulated data) as well as *in-vitro* (testing mutations in the lab, directly). I implemented a functional API into a JAX-based python package, [multidms](https://matsengrp.github.io/multidms/) [@Haddox_2023], which is now used in a primary analysis pipeline across multiple labs.

highlights.title: Bioinformatics for studying affinity maturation in germinal centers
highlights.text: Working with wet lab researchers to meet their needs, I created an efficient Nextflow pipeline that leveraged high-performance computing clusters and software containerization to perform over 50K independent data-processing steps and produce more than 140 feature-rich phylogenetic trees. This work provided the primary data and analysis for a large, collaborative study across multiple groups, since published in *Cell* [@DeWitt_2025].

highlights.title: Administrative data management
highlights.text: Executed best-practice management and storage of sensitive data in various computational environments including HPC file systems and AWS S3 buckets. Additionally, I was responsible for scrubbing sensitive data from repository histories before publication.

highlights.title: Visualization/Communication of results
highlights.text: Visualized data for researchers and produced final figures for publication to communicate patterns in data clearly. Regularly presented results and background of my research projects to a range of audiences including lab meetings, collaborative meetings, and team meetings.

title: Bioinformatics Analyst II
details: Public Health Sciences Division · Matsen Lab
summary: Designed an algorithm that estimates fitness over time for every codon mutation across a phylogeny of 13M+ viral genomes. Built and deployed public Nextstrain views of antibody escape for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and Lassa virus. Mentored interns, students, and postdocs in ML and computational methods.

highlights.title: Algorithmic design for mutational fitness estimation
highlights.text: Designed and implemented an algorithm, packaged as a Snakemake pipeline, that estimates fitness trajectories over time for every possible codon mutation across a phylogeny (evolutionary history) of more than 13 million viral genomes.

highlights.title: Genomic surveillance of viral escape
highlights.text: Built and deployed custom, public Nextstrain pages for viruses such as [SARS-CoV-2](https://nextstrain.org/groups/dms-phenotype/ncov/Dadonaite-2023-Cell), Influenza, Lassa, and others — each of which provide estimates of viral escape to antibodies of interest. This work has provided analysis tools for various studies and informed the potential effectiveness of these antibodies as therapeutics.

highlights.title: Colleague consultation
highlights.text: Mentored undergraduate interns, graduate students, and postdocs, and onboarded new staff, on machine learning, algorithm implementation, HPC clusters, workflow management, version control, compute environments, and build systems.

title: Research Associate
details: Paid Internship · Computational Biology · Matsen Lab
summary: Built phippery, a PhIP-Seq analysis suite (Nextflow pipeline, Python API for normalization and enrichment statistics, Streamlit app) used in six collaborative publications. Co-developed torchdms, a PyTorch package for neural-network global epistasis models. Led cross-lab team meetings.

highlights.title: PhIP-Seq software and analysis
highlights.text: Developed a suite of software tools, [phippery](https://matsengrp.github.io/phippery/introduction.html), for analysis of raw Phage ImmunoPrecipitation Sequencing (PhIP-Seq) data that consisted of a python package for modeling and computing enrichment statistics, an interactive application for visualizing results of the processed data, and an end-to-end (raw data → results) Nextflow pipeline for encapsulating the standard analysis workflows in a portable and reproducible manner. Multiple collaborative publications have used this software to process data and produce results [@Garrett_2022, @Stoddard_2021, @Garrett_2021, @Stoddard_2023, @Willcox_2022, @Itell_2021].

highlights.title: Neural Networks for global epistasis modeling
highlights.text: Co-developed [torchdms](https://github.com/matsengrp/torchdms) with a graduate student: a PyTorch package that fits neural-network global epistasis models to deep mutational scanning data.

highlights.title: Team Organization
highlights.text: Set up and led team meetings to brainstorm, set short-term goals, and present results across multiple labs and studies for various team members.

title: Graduate Teaching Fellow
details: BIO 410/510 · Biology Department · UO Graduate School
summary: Taught graduate-level Python/Bash scripting and algorithmic thinking. Built Docker containers and a Jupyter Notebook auto-grading pipeline. Led discussions and graded about 100 assignments per week.

highlights.title: Teaching
highlights.text: Led discussions, taught lessons, and proctored exams for four classroom hours each week for a graduate-level class focused on Python/Bash scripting, Unix file formatting/parsing, and other algorithmic thinking activities.

highlights.title: Assignment Design
highlights.text: Constructed Docker containers and a Jupyter Notebook auto-grade pipeline for students to have a unified environment for Python programming. Hosted office hours and graded ≈ 100 assignments/exams per week with feedback.

title: Scientific Programmer
details: Institute of Ecology and Evolution · Ralph & Kern Co-Lab
summary: Trained and evaluated recurrent neural networks on simulated genomes to estimate recombination rates (ReLERNN). Brought software engineering practice (architecture, version control, CI) to open-source tools including tskit and stdpopsim, and built Snakemake pipelines for published analyses.

highlights.title: Software Engineering
highlights.text: Leveraged software engineering best practices such as architecture design, version control, and continuous integration for various open-source software projects, including [tskit](https://tskit.dev/), [stdpopsim](https://popsim-consortium.github.io/stdpopsim-docs/stable/index.html), and [ReLERNN](https://github.com/kr-colab/ReLERNN).

highlights.title: Experimentation and model development
highlights.text: Trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) on simulated data to predict recombination rates across the genomes of real populations, and evaluated how well they transfer. This work provided the analysis pipeline for the resulting publication [@Adrion_2020_relernn].

highlights.title: Analysis of population demography inference tools
highlights.text: Constructed a snakemake pipeline for published analysis outlining a comparison of population demography inference tools [@Adrion_2020_stdpopsim].

title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
details: Institute of Ecology and Evolution · Ralph & Kern Co-Lab
summary: Implemented tree-sequence recording in the SLiM population genetics simulator and benchmarked its speed and memory use for an honors thesis. Led a published simulation study of rapid evolution in stickleback fish.

highlights.title: Algorithmic implementation of tree sequence recording
highlights.text: Implemented tree sequence recording algorithm into widely used population genetic simulation software, [SLiM](https://messerlab.org/slim/), and contributed to the writing in the resulting publication [@Haller_2019].

highlights.title: Algorithmic benchmarking
highlights.text: Utilized cluster resources, visualization tools, and more to compare large-scale simulations and benchmark performance across various metrics, including memory allocation and user runtime. This work was written up and formally presented in my [undergraduate honors thesis](https://www.cs.uoregon.edu/Reports/UG-201806-Galloway.pdf) and used to inform ongoing studies.

highlights.title: Simulation studies of rapid evolution
highlights.text: Developed and analyzed large-scale, realistic evolutionary simulation models to study migration patterns involved in the rapid evolution of stickleback fish on the Alaskan coast. I then led the publication of this study [@Galloway_2020].

title: Discrete Math Course Grader
summary: Graded weekly discrete math assignments focused on proofs, set theory, and combinatorics.

highlights.title: Grading
highlights.text: Graded and constructed feedback for ≈ 100 weekly assignments focused on proofs, set theory, and combinatorics.
